punchline: Ford's engineers kept telling him the one-block V-8 couldn't be built, and he kept telling them to keep going until they built it.
thirty_sec: Napoleon Hill tells how Henry Ford wanted an eight-cylinder engine cast in one block. His engineers said it was impossible. Ford said to produce it anyway, and after months of failures they found a way. Hill's larger point is that most ideas die from fear of criticism, often from friends and family, not from real obstacles. His fix is to share your plans only with a small group of trusted allies.
question: Is there an idea you've put on hold that's really just waiting for someone else's permission?
